question: What is the primary cellular change that occurs in cervical erosion (ectropion)?

options.B: Columnar epithelium extends outward to cover the ectocervix
options.C: Adipose tissue replaces the endocervical glands
options.D: Complete necrosis of the entire cervix

explanation: Cervical ectropion happens when the single-layered columnar epithelium from the endocervical canal extends outward onto the ectocervix, replacing the normal squamous epithelium. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why does cervical ectropion often appear red and ulcer-like during a speculum examination?

options.A: Due to active hemorrhage from deep tissue lacerations
options.B: Because the single-layered columnar cells allow underlying blood vessels to show through
options.C: As a result of severe fungal infection and tissue necrosis
options.D: Due to the absence of any blood supply to the cervix

explanation: The columnar epithelium is only a single layer thick, which makes underlying blood vessels visible and gives the area a red, inflamed appearance. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Which type of epithelium normally lines the endocervical canal?
explanation: The endocervical canal is normally lined by a single layer of mucus-secreting columnar epithelium, unlike the ectocervix which has squamous epithelium. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: What anatomical term describes the area where the squamous and columnar epithelia meet?
explanation: The meeting point between the squamous epithelium of the ectocervix and the columnar epithelium of the endocervix is called the squamocolumnar junction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for stimulating the changes associated with cervical ectropion?
explanation: High levels of estrogen stimulate the proliferation and eversion of the columnar epithelium, making it a primary hormonal driver of cervical ectropion. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: Which of the following is considered a significant risk factor for developing or worsening cervical erosion?
explanation: The use of estrogen-containing combined oral contraceptive pills is a well-known risk factor that promotes the eversion of the columnar epithelium. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: What is the primary protective healing process that transforms exposed columnar epithelium back into squamous epithelium?
explanation: Squamous metaplasia is the natural healing process where reserve cells differentiate to form new stratified squamous epithelium over the exposed area. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: How do Nabothian cysts typically form during the pathophysiology of cervical healing?

options.A: From bacterial infection of the deep uterine muscle
options.B: When new squamous epithelium grows over and blocks endocervical gland openings
options.C: As a result of complete necrosis of the cervix
options.D: Due to direct trauma from surgical instruments

explanation: Nabothian cysts form when newly growing squamous tissue blocks the ducts of the underlying mucus-secreting endocervical glands, trapping secretions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: What is the most frequently reported symptom by patients who are symptomatic with cervical erosion?

options.A: Severe lower abdominal pain and high fever
options.B: Excessive, non-odorous clear or yellowish vaginal discharge
options.C: Profuse arterial hemorrhage unrelated to intercourse

explanation: Symptomatic patients commonly report leukorrhea, which is excessive clear or yellowish mucus discharge produced by the exposed columnar cells. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Why does post-coital spotting frequently occur in individuals with cervical ectropion?

options.A: The squamous epithelium is excessively thick and brittle
options.B: The delicate single-layered columnar cells and superficial blood vessels are easily traumatized
options.C: There is a complete rupture of the uterine wall
options.D: Hormones cause the cervix to undergo necrosis

explanation: The fragile columnar epithelium and exposed surface blood vessels are easily irritated and injured during sexual intercourse, leading to light bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Which diagnostic test is essential during the evaluation of cervical erosion to screen for abnormal cellular changes or malignancy?
explanation: A Pap smear is critical to screen for cervical dysplasia and rule out malignancy when evaluating a patient with a visibly altered cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying acetic acid during a colposcopic examination?

options.A: To numb the cervix and eliminate pain
options.B: To stain abnormal areas white for targeted biopsy
options.C: To permanently destroy the columnar epithelium
options.D: To lubricate the speculum for easy insertion

explanation: Applying acetic acid helps highlight abnormal cellular changes by turning suspicious areas white, guiding the practitioner in taking precise tissue biopsies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the appropriate management approach for a patient with cervical erosion who is completely asymptomatic?

options.A: Immediate surgical removal of the entire uterus
options.B: No active treatment, as it is a normal physiological variant requiring reassurance

explanation: Asymptomatic cervical erosion requires no active treatment because it is a normal variant that often resolves on its own. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which of the following interventions is an example of an ablative treatment used when conservative management fails for severe symptoms?
explanation: Cryotherapy uses freezing temperatures to destroy the problematic columnar tissue, prompting normal squamous epithelial regeneration. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: What is a potential long-term complication associated with aggressive ablative treatments for cervical erosion?

options.B: Permanent enlargement of the uterine corpus

explanation: Aggressive ablative treatments can lead to narrowing of the endocervical canal, known as cervical stenosis, as well as scar tissue formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)

question: Which critical condition must always be ruled out during the differential diagnosis of a patient presenting with a red, bleeding cervix?

options.A: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or invasive cancer

explanation: It is essential to rule out cervical dysplasia and invasive cancer, as their early visual appearance can mimic benign cervical erosion. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)
